I have been farming these 10.9 mu for 30 years. I never went to school, not even one day. But I know my land, and I know what my neighbors do. Old Zhang across the road, his wheat always looks thick and green. I watch him. If he does something, I do it too.

Right now, my 7.9 mu of winter wheat is already in the ground from last autumn. Before I planted it, I hired the rotary machine to turn the soil. I put down one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu—50 jin each mu. Now that spring is here, I will water it four times: once now while the nights are still cold, then when the wheat starts jointing, then when the ears come out, and once more when the grain is filling. I will spread half a bag of urea per mu when the wheat turns green—about 25 jin per mu. I spray twice, once for weeds and once for the bugs that come when it gets warm. Last year I got about 500 jin of wheat per mu, and this year I will do the same. I am not changing anything.

After we cut the wheat in June, I plant 7.9 mu of summer maize. I buy hybrid seeds from the shop—whatever they have that my neighbors say is good, probably Zhengdan or Jundan. I do not plough for maize. I plant it right into the wheat stubble with the no-till drill. I put half a bag of compound fertilizer in the row when I plant—30 jin per mu. Then when the maize is knee-high, I spread another half bag of urea per mu. I water three times: right after planting, when it starts to tassel, and when the ears are filling. Two sprays. Last year I got 550 jin per mu. If I do the same, I should get that again.

For cotton, I have 3 mu. Cotton needs loose soil, so I pay the tractor man to plough it deep every spring. I plant hybrid cotton seeds in April. I put one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu as the base. Then I topdress twice with urea—about 30 jin total per mu—and the dealer gave me this white potash fertilizer in a small bag, 20 jin per mu, he says it makes the bolls big. I water three times and spray four times because the bollworm and those little green bugs love cotton. I hope for about 440 jin of seed cotton per mu.

My family has six people. My husband and I do most of the work. During busy times we hire two workers from the village. My children work in the city and send money home, but fertilizer and seed prices went up again this year. Still, I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk a thin crop. If I use too little and the harvest is bad, that is a disaster—we lose everything. If I use a bit too much, it is just some yuan wasted. That is what my father taught me, and that is what I have done for 30 years.
